issue_context.title: federation: support native histograms
issue_context.body:
The (quite ancient) federation code is quite special because it tries to reconstruct the exposition format from the internal Prometheus data model, which is notably different from remote write. (Back then, we assumed that the internal data model would quickly approach the data model of the exposition format… oh well…) Therefore, we need more special code to also support native histograms in federation.

(Alternative: Declare federation deprecated, do not support native histograms there, and revamp federation with Prometheus 3.x. I hope, though, we can do better than that.)

The histogram support in federation raises an interesting question about the used format. IIRC it currently uses the usual prometheus/client_golang primitives, so it speaks both the old protobuf format as well as the conventional Prometheus text format but not yet OpenMetrics. Since Prometheus servers regularly only parse OpenMetrics and the conventional Prometheus text format, they will use the latter in federation. However, it will be hard to add native histograms to the conventional Prometheus text format, and maybe we never want to do that. Therefore, the easiest path will be to only support native histograms in federation via the old protobuf format. Since Prometheus severs supporting native histograms will also (again) support the old protobuf format (at least in the experimental state of native histograms), this should "just work". However, that's not the intended stable outcome of native histograms. Whatever happens to become the standard format in normal exposition (OM protobuf support, OM text format support, …) ultimately has to be mirrored in federation, so this might require corresponding support in prometheus/client_golang before declaring native histograms a stable feature within prometheus/prometheus.

review_comments: Perhaps add a TODO so we find it once the other protocols support native histograms?
